narrative.overview:
SlapStat looks like the room where a general manager makes the call: a desk of numbers, read under good light by someone who knows the game. The screen belongs to the data. Navy frames it (the header band of every table, the one filled button, the titles) and gold marks the figure that decides (the total a player is ranked by, the Premium edge, the medal on the best pickup). Everything else stays cool, white and grey so the numbers carry the page.

The mood is **focused, exact and sure of itself**. Confidence comes from figures that line up, columns that stay put while the page scrolls, and controls that answer at once, not from decoration. Pages are dense where the job is comparison (tables run the full 1400px and the page scrolls, not the table) and calm where the job is a decision (forms and lists sit at 1100px). Interfaces are light only.

What SlapStat is not: **generic SaaS**. No purple gradients, no glassmorphism, no illustrated blobs, no stock "dashboard" cards repeated for their own sake.
keyCharacteristics: Navy structure, gold value, one blue for links and focus; everything else cool neutral.
Inter throughout, at a 14px working size, with tabular figures in every column of numbers.
Wide tables as the signature object: navy header band, frozen rank and name, a gold total column pinned to the right on wide screens.
Flat at rest: white surfaces on a cool grey ground, hairline edges, shadows only on what floats.
Every colour that carries text is checked against WCAG 4.5:1 on the darkest surface it can land on, and the ratio is written beside the token.

rules.name: The Gold Means Value Rule
rules.body: Gold marks what counts: the ranking total, Premium, the AI projection, the top three picks. It is never decoration, never a background for text, and never on two competing things in one view.

rules.name: The Ratio Beside the Token Rule
rules.body: Every colour that carries text is checked against the darkest surface it can land on, and the ratio is written in the comment beside it in `styles.css`. Lightening a text colour means rechecking that number first.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue Line is for links, the active place in navigation and focus. A second blue for anything else (a chart, a badge, a highlight) blurs what is clickable.

rules.name: The Fourteen-Pixel Rule
rules.body: The app works at 14px (0.875rem). 16px is for reading copy on public pages, 12px for labels and chips. A new screen that sets its body at 16px is the odd one out.

rules.name: The Straight Column Rule
rules.body: Figures use tabular numerals and right-align, and a column's heading ends on the same vertical line as its values (`--stat-value-inset`, shared by header, cell and input). A heading that drifts off its numbers is a bug.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Rule
rules.body: A strong shadow means "this is above the page". Cards and panels stay at Resting or Card; a card that lifts itself to Floating competes with every menu.

dos: **Do** use the `:root` custom properties for every colour, space, radius and shadow; a hex in a component stylesheet is a leftover, not a precedent.
**Do** keep one filled Rink Navy button per view; everything else is secondary, quiet or a link.
**Do** spend gold only on value: the ranking total, Premium, the AI projection, the best picks.
**Do** set every column of numbers in tabular figures, right-aligned, with the heading ending on the values' line.
**Do** give every control a visible answer to hover and focus (the 2px Focus Blue ring, 2px out), and give new controls a pressed state too.
**Do** check a new text colour against the darkest surface it can land on and write the ratio beside the token.
**Do** check every screen at 375px; the breakpoint is 640px.
donts: **Don't** use purple gradients, glassmorphism, illustrated blobs or other generic SaaS dressing.
**Don't** put a strong shadow on anything that does not float over the page.
**Don't** draw an icon by hand, type a character where an icon belongs, or add a second icon set.
**Don't** introduce a second blue for anything but links, the active place and focus.
**Don't** set app body text at 16px or headings in a second typeface.
**Don't** let a value the app does not know render as a zero or a default; a dash or no marker says "unknown".
